To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a new, more efficient fixpoint based encoding of LTL formulas to SAT is presented, 2) the encoding is implemented in a tool called fixsat, 3) fixsat is used in a bounded model checking tool called fixbmc, and 4) fixbmc outperforms the state-of-the-art tool NuSMV on several benchmarks.

(1) a new encoding for the LTL model checker is introduced that makes use of the fixpoint correspondence, (2) the new encoding is shown to result in improved performance on the SAT solver, and (3) the new encoding can be used to improve the performance of the Bounded Model Checking algorithm.

1) the encoding of a formula in the form of a predicate transformer is more compact than the encoding in the form of an implication graph and 2) the encoding of the predicate transformer in conjunctive normal form is more compact than its encoding in disjunctive normal form.

a new approach to the LTI model checking problem based on an encoding of the problem to Boolean satisfiability.
the development of a new encoding to SAT for the LTL model-checking problem.
the development of an efficient and scalable encoding of bounded model checking for LTL that is based on the fixpoint representation of LTL formulas.

the use of fixpoints can be a useful technique in the design of encodings for the Bounded Model Checking problem, particularly in the presence of complex temporal logic expressions.
